Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, criticizing the lack of mechanistic follow-up and noting recent work on OspC effectors suggests more investigation needed.

Both support the T3SS activity findings (C44-C46, C67). OpenEval provides detailed validation of the TSAR reporter system and notes statistical significance while acknowledging the antimicrobial role inference remains correlative. Peer reviewers accept these as important contributions to understanding septin cage roles.

Both support infection heterogeneity findings (C17-C20, C57-C58). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from high-content microscopy with appropriate statistical tests and multiple replicates. Peer reviewers accept these as valid descriptive characterization, with the editor noting 'important findings' acquired.

Both support findings on bacterial metabolism heterogeneity (C42-C43). OpenEval notes the data challenges uniform metabolic arrest notions and validates antibiotic controls. Peer reviewers accept the correlation between caging and bacterial metabolic activity as a valid outcome.

Both support morphological observations (C21-C25). OpenEval notes these are part of converging evidence with appropriate controls including latrunculin B experiments. Peer reviewers accept these without critique, noting 'cell biology-based approaches' as a strength.
